_README: PLACEHOLDER ITEM BANK — replace with the real prototype 5-item / 5-domain set. This file is the ONLY thing to swap; the engine, gateway and scorer read it generically. Each item is bilingual (en/sw, Section 7) and phrased to degrade to plain text so it works on USSD too (Section 3.4). Open-ended items feed the LLM Scoring Service (Section 3.3); their `expected_reasoning` is guidance for the scorer, never shown to the child. `session_intro` states the untimed, no-penalty framing explicitly (UDL practice for ADHD/anxiety) rather than leaving it unstated.

session_intro.en: There is no time limit and no penalty for skipping a question, just answer in your own way. Some questions have no single right answer, we want to see how you think.
session_intro.sw: Hakuna muda uliowekwa na hakuna adhabu kwa kuruka swali, jibu kwa njia yako. Maswali mengine hayana jibu moja sahihi, tunataka kuona jinsi unavyofikiri.

prompt.en: A shopkeeper buys 12 oranges for 60 shillings and sells them for 8 shillings each. How much profit does she make, and how did you work it out?
prompt.sw: Mwuzaji ananunua machungwa 12 kwa shilingi 60 na anauza kila moja kwa shilingi 8. Anapata faida kiasi gani, na ulifikiaje jibu hilo?

items.expected_reasoning: Cost 60, revenue 12*8=96, profit 36. Credit correct method even if arithmetic slips; note whether the child shows the per-unit vs total reasoning.

prompt.en: Rain is to farmer as ____ is to fisherman. Pick the best fit: (a) a net, (b) a hat, (c) a boat, (d) a market. Say the letter. If you want, you can also explain why, but that is optional.
prompt.sw: Mvua ni kwa mkulima kama ____ ilivyo kwa mvuvi. Chagua inayofaa zaidi: (a) wavu, (b) kofia, (c) mashua, (d) soko. Sema herufi. Ukitaka, unaweza pia kueleza sababu, lakini si lazima.

items.expected_reasoning: Redesigned as forced-choice-plus-optional-explain: research on autism and figurative language finds the group difference concentrates specifically in tasks that require explicitly constructing and explaining a metaphor mapping, not in reaching the correct meaning itself. Correct answer is (a) a net, the tool the fisherman depends on the way a farmer depends on rain. Give full base credit for the letter alone if it is (a) or a defensible alternative with sound reasoning (e.g. (c) a boat, reasoned as 'a boat is what lets a fisherman work at all'); an explanation, if given, is bonus evidence of reasoning depth, never required for base credit.

prompt.en: What number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___ ? Tell me the rule you found.
prompt.sw: Ni nambari gani inayofuata: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___ ? Nieleze kanuni uliyoipata.

items.expected_reasoning: Differences 4,6,8,10 -> next diff 12 -> 42. Reward articulating the growing-difference rule even if final number is off.

prompt.en: All the children who passed the test studied. Amina did not study. Can we be sure Amina failed? Explain your answer.
prompt.sw: Watoto wote waliofaulu mtihani walisoma. Amina hakusoma. Je, tunaweza kuwa na uhakika kwamba Amina alishindwa? Eleza jibu lako.

items.expected_reasoning: Logically we cannot be certain: studying is necessary-for-passing only as stated ('all who passed studied' => not studying implies not passing). Actually this DOES imply Amina failed. Score whether the child reasons about the conditional correctly; strongest answers notice the direction of implication.

prompt.en: Read this list once: mango, chair, river, seven, blue. Now, without looking back, write them in reverse order and tell me any trick you used to remember.
prompt.sw: Soma orodha hii mara moja: embe, kiti, mto, saba, bluu. Sasa, bila kuangalia nyuma, ziandike kwa mpangilio wa kinyume na unieleze mbinu uliyotumia kukumbuka.

items.expected_reasoning: Score recall accuracy and, more importantly, any strategy described (chunking, story, visualisation) — strategy use is a stronger giftedness signal than raw recall.
